subject: Procurement path choice — AWS Marketplace interest vs PO/card (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@nimbus.ai>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap: procurement path options we discussed (post-call)

Thanks again for taking time today — short recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Pleasure speaking with you both.

Notes from the call:
- Goal: pilot Redwood inference on a scoped set of internal features (300k tokens/mo initially) to reduce latency on search & summaries.
- Procurement preferences: Priya mentioned they default to corporate card for pilots but procurement wants PO for multi-month commitments; legal prefers marketplace where possible to reuse existing SaaS terms.
- Timeline: target pilot kickoff in early September (internal approval by Aug 15).

Options we flagged on the call (high-level):
1) Direct contract + PO to Redwood (fast for procurement if PO process is standard)
2) Card payment for initial month(s) while procurement processes PO for multi-month commit
3) AWS Marketplace (Private Offer) — buys through AWS with Marketplace billing; helps procurement reuse marketplace playbook but adds 2–3 week onboarding with AWS sales/legal for a Private Offer

Asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm whether your procurement team requires a PO for any commitment >30 days, or only for contractual commitments? (Priya — quick confirm)
- If Marketplace is preferred, who is the AWS contact or procurement owner we should loop in to start the Private Offer intake?
- I attached a short procurement checklist and a draft SOW to help procurement evaluate (see attachments).

I'll follow up with a quick one-pager comparing PO vs Marketplace impact on invoicing and timelines. Happy to jump on a 20-min call with procurement/legal if that helps.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: Nimbus-MAP-Procurement-Checklist.pdf (procurement checklist, 2 pages); SOW-draft-v1.docx (scope + pilot milestones)
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@nimbus.ai>

Date: Sun, 20 Jul 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap: procurement path options we discussed (post-call)

Thanks for the clear summary, Avery — useful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement policy: for pilots where we commit a funding line (even month-to-month) procurement wants a PO if the cumulative spend is expected to exceed $10k/month. For very short proof-of-concepts (<30 days) they accept card.
- Marketplace preference: legal likes Marketplace because it avoids bespoke contract redlines, but the AWS Private Offer workflow is unfamiliar to our procurement lead and they worry about lead time.

Questions:
1) If we go Marketplace Private Offer, can Redwood do a standard Marketplace SOW (we'd rather avoid heavyweight custom SOW negotiations)?
2) Timing: you said Private Offer onboarding typically adds 2–3 weeks — is that from initiation with your team or from when AWS begins intake?

Priya, can you confirm whether we should kick off a Private Offer intake or proceed with a PO?

Onward,
Sanjay
Head of Product, Nimbus AI
sanjay.rao@nimbus.ai

Appreciate the fast reply, Sanjay — answers inline below plus proposed immediate actions.

1) Marketplace SOW: Redwood supports a lightweight Marketplace SOW template that maps to the Private Offer billing item. We normally include pilot milestones and SLAs but keep legal terms standard to avoid redlines. I attached the draft SOW to this thread for procurement's review.

2) Timing: Private Offer onboarding typically follows this cadence:
   - Redwood initiates POA with AWS and generates the Private Offer item (1–3 business days)
   - AWS conducts a quick intake (1–2 business days) — overall 2–5 business days before the Private Offer is visible in your account (in practice it can be faster, but allow up to a week if AWS is busy).

High-level recommendation based on your timeline:
- If Nimbus needs to start the pilot in early September and procurement approval is expected by Aug 15, we recommend starting the Marketplace intake now in parallel with procurement's PO process. That keeps options open and can reduce final friction.

Immediate asks from your side:
- Priya: please share procurement lead contact (name + email) so we can loop them in on the intake.
- Sanjay: confirm expected monthly run-rate for the pilot (ballpark $k/month) so we can draft a Private Offer amount and a PO-friendly invoice cadence.

I'll also attach a short one-pager comparing "direct PO" vs "Marketplace Private Offer" on invoicing cadence, legal friction, and typical lead time.

Happy to set a 20-min alignment call this week with procurement. When's best for your team?

Best,
